source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.Download the opembmc-tools on Git-hub : https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc-tools/tree/master/
2.Install openbmc tool
2. Send command : ./openbmctool  -H $BMCIP -U root -P 0penBmc ldap enable --uri="ldaps://<ldap server IP/hostname>" --bindDN=<bindDN> --baseDN=<basDN> --bindPassword=<bindPassword> --scope="sub/one/base" --serverType="OpenLDAP/ActiveDirectory"
a) It is quite common to encounter the following error when running the openbmctool.py command string shown above:
>> xyz.openbmc_project.Common.Error.NoCACertificate
-- This error means that the BMC client needs to verify that the LDAP server's certificate has been signed by a known CA. The service action would be for the admin to upload the CA certificate to the BMC.
-- To upload the CA certificate to the BMC, refer to the "Update LDAP root certificate" section of this document.
b) openbmctool doesn't support individual LDAP config property update, To update a single property user need to recreate the LDAP config with the changed values.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: openbmctool.py (openbmc-tools, install) + LDAP server + CA certificate (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Secure Create LDAP Configuration (Secure LDAP config): `openbmctool ${BMC_CONN:?operator must supply openbmctool target, e.g. http://${BMC_USER}:${BMC_PASS}@${BMC_IP}:8080/} ldap enable --uri="ldaps://${LDAP_SERVER:?operator must supply the LDAP server FQDN/IP}"` + upload the CA cert (user provides the cert file). Agent runs it when the certificate is in place and verifies success.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the openbmctool output + cert-upload status so the user confirms the Secure/ldaps LDAP config + cert uploaded (note: FQDN must match the cert to avoid hostname errors).
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: enabling Secure LDAP with a wrong cert/FQDN can break BMC auth; supply the correct cert + FQDN.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires an isolated approved directory, pinned tool, protected secrets, DNS/SAN/chain/TLS and active CA validation, a complete replacement payload, positive/negative/role/local-fallback tests and rollback.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC can establish a secure `ldaps://` configuration through openbmctool after trusting the approved LDAP CA, with correct directory search/server semantics, certificate hostname validation, expected authentication and role mapping, and retained local recovery.
original_method: Pin and review openbmctool; preserve the complete BMC auth/LDAP/CA state and independent recovery; verify BMC DNS/route and the LDAPS server certificate SAN, chain, validity and TLS policy; upload the approved CA through the specified supported path; create the complete LDAP object once with protected secrets; read back state and prove secure positive/negative authentication, mapping and local fallback; then restore or retain the approved state.
manual_activity: A security owner approves the LDAPS endpoint, CA, complete directory semantics, role matrix, tool version, secret path and recovery. A human controls the CA trust-store write and full LDAP-object creation, retains independent local access, verifies login behavior and restores or accepts final state. Automation may perform redacted validation after point-of-action approval.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity and supported pinned openbmctool/API version
Approved LDAPS server FQDN/port, DNS/route and server certificate/full chain
Approved CA certificate/chain, fingerprint, format and vendor upload/active-store method
Bind DN, base DN, scope, serverType and complete replacement payload
Expected allowed/denied user/group/role mapping and local-admin fallback
Current auth/LDAP/CA policy export and independent console recovery
safety_requirements: Do not use the literal `root`/`0penBmc`, expose bind/BMC credentials or private keys in command lines, URLs, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review records.
Verify the exact CA fingerprint/chain and LDAPS hostname/SAN before upload. Never bypass certificate verification or accept an IP URI unless the certificate and Project policy explicitly cover it.
Do not clear security/audit logs. Preserve the complete prior auth/LDAP/CA configuration and verify independent local-admin/console recovery before any trust or auth change.
Because the tool may recreate the entire LDAP object, compare every property and obtain approval for the full replacement, not merely one changed field.
Obtain separate point-of-action approval for the CA-store write and one complete LDAPS configuration write; do not retry or remove other trust anchors on error.
Stop on NoCACertificate, wrong CA/SAN/chain/TLS, target mismatch, unexpected role, local fallback failure, lockout, insecure downgrade or inability to restore.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the target, pinned tool, BMC-to-LDAPS DNS/route, certificate/CA/TLS, full payload, secrets, auth matrix, baseline and recovery; present the exact CA and LDAP actions for approval.

After approval, upload only the approved CA, verify active trust state, then create one complete secure LDAP configuration using protected secret injection and capture redacted audit/readback evidence.
Prove certificate validation, allowed and denied LDAP authentication, group/role mapping and independent local-admin fallback without clearing logs.
Disable/restore or preserve the explicitly approved state, confirm access, archive redacted evidence and stop without TLS bypass, partial blind recreation, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint/server certificate/CA fingerprint and upload method, pinned tool, complete LDAP payload, roles and protected secret handling.
Approve the CA write, one full-object create/recreate, service impact, local recovery and final restore/retention state.
Review trust, configuration, auth, audit and recovery evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies LDAPS and a CA file but omits source fields that determine configuration, uses credential-bearing URL syntax, does not establish the supported CA action or active trust, and cannot prove authentication from output/status. The preserved source command also contains unsafe default-looking credentials and command-line bind secret.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the pinned vendor openbmctool `ldap enable` path and every source LDAP field after approved CA installation, but use reviewed protected credential injection and a verified FQDN/SAN; treat any property update as a newly approved full replacement.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool install, `ldaps://` URI, bind/base DN, scope choices, serverType choices, NoCACertificate behavior, CA-upload reference, full-recreate caveat, source credentials, Criteria, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved as evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate and install one approved CA, then apply one fully reviewed LDAPS object and prove live TLS trust, positive/negative authentication, role mapping, local fallback and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC LDAP and CA trust-store implementation against the approved lab LDAP/AD service.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime, directory server and TLS client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools source/docs, vendor LDAP/CA-store schema, Project PKI/authentication policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Protects secrets, pins dependencies, validates active CA/TLS and tests authentication/recovery while retaining the source CA upload and full-recreate semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Cleartext LDAP is the preceding row; CA upload alone does not prove LDAPS auth; a vendor API override must record uncovered openbmctool behavior; command acceptance does not prove roles or fallback.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Endpoint/certificate/CA, pinned tool, full LDAP object, secrets, auth matrix, baseline and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong CA, FQDN, chain, TLS policy or full replacement can break authentication or overwrite settings; trust-store changes can affect more than LDAP.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor API or WebUI only when it records the original openbmctool and referenced CA-upload methods, actual methods, reason, engineer approval, trust/config/auth equivalence and uncovered tool/UI coverage. It may not downgrade to `ldap://` or disable verification.
expected_evidence: Approved target/change window, BMC/firmware, pinned tool, complete redacted prior auth/LDAP/CA state and independent local recovery
BMC DNS/route plus LDAPS server SAN/chain/validity/TLS evidence and approved CA fingerprint/format
One CA upload/active-store audit and one complete redacted openbmctool configuration/audit/readback tied to the intended endpoint and properties
Verified certificate enforcement, allowed LDAP login, denied login, group/role mapping and separate local-admin fallback
Full-state comparison and disable/restore or approved retained-state proof, preserved logs/no secret exposure/no retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require secure LDAPS creation, handling NoCACertificate through an approved LDAP CA upload, and command/certificate success. The missing exact CA-upload action and Project-specific endpoints are execution-readiness inputs rather than competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The secure LDAP, CA-trust and authentication objective is identifiable. Vendor documentation and Project inputs can define the tool revision, CA path, full payload and recovery, so missing artifacts make execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but restores all source LDAP fields, removes credential-bearing shorthand, proves CA activation/TLS/auth behavior and manages full-object recreation and recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its critical security controls and explicitly separates CA-store acceptance, complete LDAP-object creation and independent live authentication checkpoints.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic output/status evidence with cryptographic trust, full-state and login/role/local-recovery evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps non-secure LDAP separate and retains Delete LDAP Config as later disable coverage rather than accepting either as secure-create proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents TLS bypass, secret leakage, wrong-CA trust and authentication lockout while proving the actual secure LDAP function instead of merely accepting a tool response.
independent_technical_reasoning: Secure LDAP has two coupled state changes: the BMC trust store must accept the intended CA, and the directory object must use a hostname whose served certificate chains to it with the correct search and role semantics. Either command can succeed while live TLS or authentication fails. Because property edits recreate the object, evidence must compare the full payload and retain local recovery before proving real login behavior.
